docs.title: Advanced — 8 Tips for Parallel, Autonomous, Scheduled Work
docs.summary: Eight tips for parallel, autonomous, scheduled work, plus self-approval bias — collision-free parallel sessions with claude --worktree, calling APIs directly instead of MCP (context cost), the three tiers of scheduling (/loop, desktop tasks, cloud Routines), phone remote control, natural-language database queries, ultrathink and OMC's consensus-based ralplan, editing permissions in settings.json (auto mode's hard denies), and subagents vs agent teams (plus OMC's team mode). The rationale for splitting roles is self-preference bias — the ability to recognize one's own output correlates linearly with favoring it, and a single agent running plan→execute→verify turns that bias into a loop. docs.name: sks-dews-sourcegraph
docs.title: dews-sourcegraph — A Skill That Hands Internal Code Search to Claude
docs.summary: A skill that lets Claude Code query an in-house SourceGraph instance directly. A private instance blocks anonymous access with a 401, so an ordinary web-fetch tool reads nothing — this skill performs a browser form login once on its own, using the Edge or Chrome already installed on the machine, and caches the session for reuse, which removes the step of copying cookies out of DevTools. It explains why the downloadable cache browser is avoided (on corporate machines a security agent blocks the ms-playwright executable, and the browser then hangs without even painting a blank page), the install that ends with merging .claude into the project root, three lines in SourceGraph.md and npm install, the standard Sourcegraph query filters, and the local-first rule with the [SG repo/file:line] citation convention. Two prohibitions are nailed down — never commit the credentials file or the session cache, and never retry a failed login, because repeated password failures lock the account. A generalized zip with all organization-specific values stripped is available for download.

docs.summary: Three early-September items about Claude usage, bound into one frame. An infostealer copied login session cookies and spent other people's limits (two-factor authentication guards only the moment of logging in; Anthropic signed accounts out, deleted saved payment methods and refunded charges identified as unauthorized; the named families are Vidar, LummaC2, StealC, RedLine and Acreed plus Atomic Stealer on a small number of Macs; signing out does not remove the malware). On September 14 Claude Code's weekly limit replaces a temporary 50% boost with a permanent 25% increase, a net drop of roughly 17% against today's limit, which is why the same change is written as both +25% and -17%. Claude Code 2.1.251 added a spend-limit bar and a per-session prompt-cache line to /usage plus PreModelSwitch and PostModelSwitch hooks. Three sides of one meter: who spends it, how much is left, and what shows it

docs.title: Doors on the Model — Who May Use It, and How You May Call It
docs.summary: Two changes two days apart, bound into one frame. Google released Gemini 3.8 Flash (90.8% on Terminal-Bench 2.1, $0.75 per million input tokens and $3.75 per million output) but kept the sibling 3.8 Flash Cyber off the API, opening it only through the Fairwind program to government authorities, critical-infrastructure operators and software maintainers who pass an identity review (86.2% on CyberGym is a public C/C++ evaluation, the 70%-plus rate across 20 languages is Google's own testing, and the Chrome team reported 2.6 times more correct patches). Anthropic put conditions on the call in Fable 5.1: forcing a tool with tool_choice any or tool now returns a 400 and is replaced by a role: system message plus strict: true, and a thinking block is valid only for the model that produced it and only against the system prompt, tool list and history that preceded it, so editing history invalidates it (enforced by default only for accounts created on or after 2026-08-31, with prefix_mismatch_behavior and input_transformations to test and soften it). Two ways of tying a capability to the conditions that produced it
